name: Dexterous hand, 17 DOF
description: Tendon-driven hand with 17 degrees of freedom: wrist rotation and pitch; per finger spread, knuckle flex and middle flex with the tip following the middle joint; thumb opposition, base flex and middle flex. Fifteen SG90s in a printed bed reel flexor and extensor lines through PTFE sheaths; two more drive the wrist directly.

hardware.note: one per hinge, lengths as drawn; 2.4 mm clearance holes
usually supplied with the SG90; measure your servo's tab hole spacing and drill the bed
one run per tendon, from the spool groove to the anchor eyelet
3 mm OD; cut one sheath per tendon from its bed stop to the palm

notes: Each servo carries a printed two-groove spool: the flexor winds on one groove, the extensor on the other, so the servo pulls the joint both ways. Spool radii are fitted so the line the spool takes up matches what the joints take up over their range; the lab shows the remaining slack or stretch of every line.

Lines run on the palm side (flexors) and the back (extensors) through eyelets; the middle-joint lines cross the knuckle next to its pin, so flexing the knuckle hardly pulls them. Tips follow the middle joints by fixed ratios (0.7 fingers, 0.9 thumb), standing in for a coupling the tendon alone does not set.
Not simulated: line stretch, friction in the sheaths and eyelets, grip force.
17 servos need their own 5 V supply (the template uses a bench supply) with its ground shared by both boards.
The SG90 pockets are the case outline plus 0.2 mm per side; the tab screw holes are not in a drawing we could read — mark them from your servos.
Board U1 drives flexion and the thumb (11 servos), U2 spread and wrist (6): the Arduino Servo library runs at most 12 servos on an Uno.
